title: Holiday tuition: know the rules and handle it responsibly
description: A practical guide for Kenyan school principals on navigating Ministry of Education guidance on holiday tuition, and on offering learning support without breaching the rules.
body:
Every year, as the holidays approach, parents ask whether the school will run holiday tuition, and some teachers ask to organise it. It is also an area where schools run into trouble with education officers. Knowing the current rules before you say yes is the safest approach.

This is general guidance, not legal advice. Rules are set through Ministry of Education circulars, and they change, so always confirm the current position with your Sub-County Director of Education before organising anything.

Why holiday tuition is regulated

Education authorities in Kenya have repeatedly issued directives restricting tuition during school holidays, particularly in public schools. The reasoning usually includes learner rest and wellbeing, the extra financial burden on parents, and fairness between families who can and cannot pay.

Principals should assume that unapproved paid tuition carries real risk, for the school, the BOM, and individual teachers.

Before anyone organises anything

  • Obtain and read the latest Ministry of Education circular on tuition and holiday programmes.
  • Confirm in writing with the Sub-County Director of Education what, if anything, your school may offer.
  • Take any proposal to the BOM so that the decision is a governance decision, not a staffroom arrangement.
  • Never charge parents for any holiday programme without explicit written approval.

Protect your teachers: A teacher who runs informal paid tuition against a circular exposes themselves to disciplinary action. A clear written school position, shared with all staff before the holiday, protects them as much as the school.

Legitimate alternatives

Even where tuition is not allowed, schools can support learning without breaching the rules: holiday assignments linked to next term, library borrowing, reading lists, and parent guidance notes. Where learners form their own study groups, the school can encourage it without organising or charging for it.

Communicating clearly with parents

Parents who hear nothing assume the school is doing something or is being unhelpful. A short, plain message explaining the school's position, what is not permitted and why, and what the school is offering instead, prevents rumours and pressure.

Keep school notices clear and on record.
